previous_assumption: Any non-2xx API response reaching a page's catch block was assumed to represent a genuine failure worth showing in a red ErrorState banner.
correction: Several backend "find the current X for Y" endpoints (e.g. `GET /organizations/:id/requirement-discovery/:requirementId/auction`, backing `getActiveAuctionForRequirement`) correctly 404 when the resource simply doesn't exist yet — a normal, expected state (a Requirement with no auction started), not an error. `RentalCompanyAuctionPanel` in auctions/page.tsx was passing that 404's message straight into `setError`, showing "Auction not found" in a scary red banner directly above the already-correct "No auction running" EmptyState. Fixed by adding a `status: number` field to `ApiError` (apps/web/lib/api-client.ts, populated from `response.status` in `apiRequest`) so callers can distinguish "not found" (silently treated as empty state) from a genuine failure (network/permission/500, still shown as an error). When adding a new "fetch a single resource that may legitimately not exist yet" call on the frontend, check `err instanceof ApiError && err.status === 404` before surfacing `err.message` as an ErrorState — don't assume every caught error is worth alarming the user about.
